chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ali Al-Jawwani, who said:

I witnessed Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) while he was saying to a slave of his called Saalim, and he placed his hand on his lips and said: 'O Saalim! Preserve your tongue and you will be safe, and do not load the people upon our necks.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of preserving the tongue according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructs his freed slave Salim to guard his tongue, linking linguistic restraint directly to spiritual safety (salama). The gesture of placing his hand on his lips underscores the physical discipline required for verbal piety, while the phrase 'do not burden us with the necks of people' highlights the concept of *al-haml 'ala al-riqab*, where the Imams bear the responsibility for the community's conduct and are held accountable for their followers' actions.

en.hubeali: From him, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abu Ali Al Jawwany who said,

‘I witnessed Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> was saying to a slave of his<sup>asws</sup> called Saalim, and he<sup>asws</sup> placed his<sup>asws</sup> hand upon his lips and said: ‘O Saalim! Preserve your tongue, you will be safe, and do not load the people upon our<sup>asws</sup> necks’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from abu Ali al-Jawwani who has said the following:

“I saw abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) speaking to one of his slaves called Salim, placing his hands over his (slaves) mouth, ‘O Salim, control your tongue and you will have peace and do not load people over our necks.’”
